review.title: Time limit for ratifying the Twenty-first Amendment
review.plain: This article is inoperative unless ratified by conventions in the several States within seven years from the date of its submission to the States by Congress.

provisions.what: This article shall be inoperative unless it shall have been ratified as an amendment to the Constitution by conventions in the several States, as provided in the Constitution, within seven years from the date of the submission hereof to the States by the Congress
conditions: unless it shall have been ratified as an amendment to the Constitution by conventions in the several States, as provided in the Constitution, within seven years from the date of the submission hereof to the States by the Congress

review.title: Two-term limit for the President
review.plain: No person shall be elected President more than twice, and no one who has held or acted as President for more than two years of another person's term shall be elected more than once. This did not apply to the President in office when it was proposed.
limits: No person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice
shall be elected to the office of the President more than once

shall not prevent any person who may be holding the office of President, or acting as President, during the term within which this Article becomes operative from holding the office of President or acting as President during the remainder of such term

review.title: Time limit for ratifying the Twenty-second Amendment
review.plain: This article is inoperative unless ratified by the legislatures of three-fourths of the several States within seven years from the date of its submission to the States by Congress.

provisions.what: This article shall be inoperative unless it shall have been ratified as an amendment to the Constitution by the legislatures of three-fourths of the several States within seven years from the date of its submission to the States by the Congress

review.title: Presidential electors for the District of Columbia
review.plain: The seat of Government of the United States appoints, as Congress directs, electors for President and Vice President equal to the Senators and Representatives it would have if a State, but no more than the least populous State.
powers: shall appoint in such manner as the Congress may direct

provisions.what: The District constituting the seat of Government of the United States shall appoint in such manner as the Congress may direct: A number of electors of President and Vice President equal to the whole number of Senators and Representatives in Congress to which the District would be entitled if it were a State, but in no event more than the least populous State
provisions.holder: The District constituting the seat of Government of the United States
requires: in such manner as the Congress may direct
but in no event more than the least populous State

provisions.what: they shall be in addition to those appointed by the States, but they shall be considered, for the purposes of the election of President and Vice President, to be electors appointed by a State; and they shall meet in the District and perform such duties as provided by the twelfth article of amendment
requires: they shall meet in the District and perform such duties as provided by the twelfth article of amendment

review.title: Power to enforce the Twenty-third Amendment
review.plain: Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: The Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

provisions.what: The Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

review.title: No poll tax in federal elections
review.plain: The right of citizens to vote in any primary or other election for President, Vice President, presidential electors, Senator or Representative shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or any State for failure to pay any poll tax or other tax.
rights: The right of citizens of the United States to vote in any primary or other election for President or Vice President, for electors for President or Vice President, or for Senator or Representative in Congress
limits: shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or any State by reason of failure to pay any poll tax or other tax

provisions.what: The right of citizens of the United States to vote in any primary or other election for President or Vice President, for electors for President or Vice President, or for Senator or Representative in Congress, shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or any State by reason of failure to pay any poll tax or other tax
provisions.binds: The United States or any State
forbids: denying or abridging the right to vote by reason of failure to pay any poll tax or other tax

review.title: Vice President becomes President
review.plain: If the President is removed from office, dies or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.

provisions.what: In case of the removal of the President from office or of his death or resignation, the Vice President shall become President
conditions: In case of the removal of the President from office or of his death or resignation

review.title: Filling a Vice President vacancy
review.plain: When the office of Vice President is vacant, the President nominates a Vice President, who takes office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.
powers: the President shall nominate a Vice President

provisions.what: Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Vice President, the President shall nominate a Vice President who shall take office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress
requires: shall take office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress
conditions: Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Vice President

review.title: President's declaration of inability
review.plain: When the President sends a written declaration to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House that he is unable to discharge his powers and duties, the Vice President discharges them as Acting President until the President declares otherwise.

provisions.what: such powers and duties shall be discharged by the Vice President as Acting President
conditions: Whenever the President transmits to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives his written declaration that he is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office
until he transmits to them a written declaration to the contrary

review.title: Declaring the President unable to serve
review.plain: If the Vice President and a majority of the principal officers of the executive departments (or another body Congress provides) declare in writing that the President is unable to serve, the Vice President becomes Acting President. Disputes are decided by Congress by two-thirds vote of both Houses.
powers: the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties of the office as Acting President

provisions.what: Whenever the Vice President and a majority of either the principal officers of the executive departments or of such other body as Congress may by law provide, transmit to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives their written declaration that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties of the office as Acting President
provisions.holder: The Vice President and a majority of either the principal officers of the executive departments or of such other body as Congress may by law provide
conditions: transmit to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives their written declaration that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office

provisions.what: when the President transmits to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives his written declaration that no inability exists, he shall resume the powers and duties of his office
exceptions: unless the Vice President and a majority of either the principal officers of the executive department or of such other body as Congress may by law provide, transmit within four days to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives their written declaration that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office

provisions.what: Thereupon Congress shall decide the issue, assembling within forty-eight hours for that purpose if not in session

provisions.what: If the Congress, within twenty-one days after receipt of the latter written declaration, or, if Congress is not in session, within twenty-one days after Congress is required to assemble, determines by two-thirds vote of both Houses that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, the Vice President shall continue to discharge the same as Acting President; otherwise, the President shall resume the powers and duties of his office

review.title: Right to vote at age eighteen
review.plain: The right of citizens of the United States who are eighteen years of age or older to vote shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of age.

review.plain: No law varying the compensation of Senators and Representatives takes effect until an election of Representatives has intervened.
